# Acute Surgery

This folder contains the core clinical quality indicators and foundational medical concepts used by the Akut Kirurgi Databasen (AKDB) to monitor and improve care for acute high-risk abdominal surgery patients. It details specific process and outcome metrics—such as timely antibiotic administration, preoperative optimization, early mobilization, epidural anesthesia, and 30- and 90-day mortality rates—alongside the defining characteristics of the target AHA population and conditions like acute abdomen. Each indicator page tracks national and regional performance against established standards, highlighting systemic challenges in patient identification, data registration, and clinical workflows across Danish healthcare regions.

## Pages

- [[aha-patienter|AHA-patienter]] — Defines the acute high-risk abdominal patient subset and highlights regional challenges in correctly identifying and referring them for timely interventions like CT scans.
- [[aha-populationen|AHA-populationen]] — Outlines the target demographic monitored by the AKDB, detailing the systemic and clinical difficulties regions face in assessing these patients upon admission.
- [[akut-abdomen|akut abdomen]] — Describes the acute abdominal condition, noting regional variations in pain management and the diagnostic challenges of identifying perforated organs.
- [[antibiotikabehandling]] — Covers the clinical intervention of antibiotic treatment and its timing, which is directly measured by the database's first process indicator.
- [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] — Tracks the proportion of patients receiving antibiotic treatment within three hours of hospital arrival, noting a national development goal of >60% and significant regional variations.
- [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] — Measures the rate of preoperative optimization or direct-to-surgery pathways within four hours, revealing low national compliance and ongoing discussions about patient inclusion criteria.
- [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]] — Evaluates the proportion of patients operated on within six hours of arrival among those operated within 24 hours, highlighting early data collection efforts and coding dependencies.
- [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] — Monitors postoperative monitoring in intermediate care units for high-risk patients (age ≥75 or ASA ≥3), showing low national adherence and missing data challenges.
- [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] — Tracks early mobilization within 24 hours post-surgery, documenting improvements linked to quality improvement teams but persistent registration hurdles.
- [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]] — Assesses whether nutritional status is addressed within 48 hours post-operation, currently undergoing redefinition to focus on actual nutritional intake rather than just care plans.
- [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] — Measures the use of epidural anesthesia during surgery, with a >60% development target that accounts for contraindications in comorbid or anticoagulated patients.
- [[indikator-9|Indikator 9]] — Tracks 30-day postoperative mortality, showing national success in staying below the <12% target and highlighting best-practice hospitals.
- [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]] — Monitors 90-day postoperative mortality, noting national compliance with the <18% target and discussions around risk-adjusting for comorbidities like cancer.
- [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] — Evaluates 90-day mortality with a strict <20% standard, identifying specific institutional outliers and data quality issues that failed to meet the benchmark.
